statement: A protocol definition constrains both Record structure and authorization semantics for Records that declare its protocol URI.
Protocol role authority is contextual; possessing a role outside the relevant protocol context must not authorize unrelated Records.
Protocol authorization evaluates the effective semantic Author, not merely the cryptographic Signer.
Historical Records must be evaluated against the governing protocol configuration for the relevant Record time, not blindly against the newest configuration.
Cross-protocol composition introduces dependency edges that must be resolved according to the referenced protocol/context rather than assumed to be local to the current protocol.
Protocol authorization to read and possession of decryption material are separate capabilities.
